identification.summary: TAG-112 is Recorded Future's Insikt Group designation for a China-nexus activity cluster that compromised two Tibetan websites, Tibet Post and Gyudmed Tantric University, in late May 2024 and used them to distribute Cobalt Strike [S1][S2]. The sites were reportedly compromised through Joomla CMS vulnerabilities and injected JavaScript that showed a fake TLS certificate error to lure visitors into downloading a disguised security certificate [S1][S2].
identification.firstObserved: Late May 2024 (compromise of the Tibetan websites), per Insikt reporting as relayed by secondary coverage [S1][S2].
identification.notes: Insikt describes TAG-112 as likely a subgroup of TAG-102 (Evasive Panda, also reported as Bronze Highland, Daggerfly, StormBamboo) but treats it as a separate entity because of the difference in maturity (less sophisticated, no custom malware observed) [S1][S3]. No Microsoft name or MITRE group ID is established in the sources gathered. Do not merge TAG-112 facts with Evasive Panda reporting.

attribution.sponsor: Insikt Group assesses TAG-112 as China-nexus; no specific PRC organization is named in the sources gathered [S1][S3].
attribution.confidence: Insikt judges TAG-112 likely a subgroup of TAG-102, working toward the same or similar intelligence requirements [S1]. The sources gathered do not state a formal confidence level beyond this wording.
attribution.basis: Infrastructure overlap with TAG-102, Cloudflare-concealed infrastructure, shared historical targeting of Tibetan entities, and tactical overlaps, per Insikt as relayed by secondary coverage [S1][S2][S3].

objectives: Insikt assesses the activity as almost certainly aimed at information collection or surveillance of Tibetan community visitors, not destruction [S4].

regions: Tibetan community; visitors of the compromised sites (geography of victims not stated in sources gathered)
targeting.notes: Compromised sites were Tibet Post and Gyudmed Tantric University [S1][S2]. Insikt's report (cut-off 3 October 2024) states the sites remained compromised and hosting the malicious JavaScript at that time [S1][S2]. Tibet Post was also separately compromised by Evasive Panda (TAG-102) in an earlier watering-hole and supply-chain operation, reported as active since at least September 2023 [S2].

capabilities.summary: Initial access to the websites is believed to be via exploitation of Joomla CMS vulnerabilities [S1][S2]. Injected JavaScript redirected visitors to an actor domain presenting a modified fake browser TLS certificate error page, prompting download of a fake security certificate that deployed Cobalt Strike [S2][S3]. One source names update[.]maskrisks[.]com as associated infrastructure [S3]. Infrastructure used Cloudflare name servers to hide the actor's IP addresses. Insikt notes no custom malware, indicating lower sophistication than TAG-102 [S1][S3].

campaigns.name: Evasive Panda (TAG-102) watering hole on Tibet Post (related, separate cluster)
campaigns.summary: The Hacker News notes Tibet Post was separately compromised by the Evasive Panda actor in a watering-hole and supply-chain attack on Tibetan users, reported as active at least since September 2023. Listed for context; not attributed to TAG-112.

campaigns.summary: TAG-112 compromised both Tibetan websites in late May 2024, reportedly via Joomla CMS vulnerabilities, and injected JavaScript to push Cobalt Strike via a fake TLS certificate error.

diamond.adversary: China-nexus cluster tracked by Insikt as TAG-112, likely a subgroup of TAG-102 [S1][S3].
diamond.capability: Joomla CMS exploitation, JavaScript injection, fake TLS certificate lure, Cobalt Strike [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Compromised legitimate Tibetan websites; actor domains fronted by Cloudflare name servers [S3].
diamond.victim: Tibet Post, Gyudmed Tantric University, and their site visitors [S1][S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Collection against the Tibetan community, consistent with Insikt's information-collection/surveillance assessment [S4].
diamond.technology: Unpatched or vulnerable Joomla CMS installations on small community websites; user trust in browser certificate warnings [S1][S2].

gaps: Could not open the primary Recorded Future Insikt report (recordedfuture.com and PDF); details here rely on search-result summaries and secondary coverage (The Hacker News, The Record, SC Media, GBHackers).
Specific Joomla CVEs, Cobalt Strike configuration, full IOC list and exact report publication day were not verified.
Number and identity of victims who downloaded the payload are unknown.
Relationship to TAG-102/Evasive Panda is assessed 'likely subgroup' by Insikt but TAG-112 is also treated as separate; no vendor cross-mapping (Microsoft, MITRE) found.
No PRC sponsoring organization is named in sources gathered.
Earlier claim that the tactic was active until early October 2024 was corrected: sources only support sites being compromised as of the 3 October 2024 report cut-off.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Small community and media websites on CMS platforms such as Joomla are the relevant terrain for this actor; they are low-cost watering holes against diaspora and civil-society audiences, with limited direct DoD relevance [S1][S2]. STEP 2: Cloudflare fronting and compromised legitimate sites reduce the defender's ability to block by reputation [S3]. STEP 3: Template is CMS exploitation, JavaScript injection, social-engineering lure (fake certificate error), Cobalt Strike beacon [S1][S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued watering-hole collection against Tibetan-interest sites. MDCOA is reuse of the same low-cost lure against sites frequented by government, coalition or regional-policy audiences. Candidate indicators: unexpected injected script on CMS pages, browser pages mimicking certificate errors that offer a file download, and Cobalt Strike beacon traffic after visits to affected sites [S1][S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track CMS-based sites visited by supported personnel and partners, and ingest Insikt/vendor IOCs once the primary report is obtained. (2) Authorities: this is third-party civil-society targeting; defensive actions are limited to DoD networks and DIB partners via normal channels. (3) Mission assurance: user training that certificate-error pages never require downloading a file, plus endpoint detection for Cobalt Strike. (4) Coordination: share indicators with partners and civil-society defenders through established intelligence-sharing channels.

provenance.importedSummary: TAG-112 is a Chinese state-sponsored APT that compromised Tibetan websites, including Tibet Post and Gyudmed Tantric University, to deliver Cobalt Strike malware. The group exploited vulnerabilities in the Joomla CMS to embed malicious JavaScript that spoofed a TLS certificate error, tricking users into downloading a compromised security certificate. TAG-112's infrastructure, concealed using Cloudflare, shows notable overlap with TAG-102, but it employs less sophisticated tactics, relying on Cobalt Strike rather than custom malware. The campaign reflects ongoing cyber-espionage efforts targeting Tibetan entities, likely for information collection and surveillance.
